title: pvRotationalExtrusion
body:
## pvRotationalExtrusion

Sweeps polygonal data around an axis through the coordinate origin (RotationAxis, ParaView default z) to build a swept surface: free edges and lines become surfaces and vertices become lines, so a profile curve becomes an axisymmetric shell (cylinder, bottle), and Translation or DeltaRadius turn it into a spring or spiral. Capping closes the ends with copies of a filled 2-D input. Output is polydata, a surface rather than a volume; use pvVolumeOfRevolution to sweep 2-D cells into volume cells.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The axis passes through (0, 0, 0); translate the profile first (transform) if the physical axis is elsewhere.
- Closed surfaces such as a sphere have no free edges, so they give no swept surface, only caps.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `RotationalExtrusion`. Identity: `filters/RotationalExtrusionFilter`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the Rotational Extrusion filter. Accepted data: polygonal data (surfaces, lines or vertices) (vtkPolyData). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPolyData"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Angle` | This property specifies the angle of rotation in degrees. The surface is swept from 0 to the value of this property. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `Capping` | If this property is set to 1, the open ends of the swept surface will be capped with a copy of the input dataset. This works property if the input is a 2D surface composed of filled polygons. If the input dataset is a closed solid (e.g., a sphere), then either two copies of the dataset will be drawn or no surface will be drawn. No surface is drawn if either this property is set to 0 or if the two surfaces would occupy exactly the same 3D space (i.e., the Angle property's value is a multiple of 360, and the values of the Translation and DeltaRadius properties are 0). | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `DeltaRadius` | The value of this property specifies the change in radius during the sweep process. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `Resolution` | The value of this property controls the number of intermediate node points used in performing the sweep (rotating from 0 degrees to the value specified by the Angle property. | `{"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `RotationAxis` | The values of this property set the direction of the axis around which the rotation is done. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `Translation` | The value of this property specifies the total amount of translation along the rotation axis during the sweep process. Specifying a non-zero value for this property allows you to create a corkscrew (value of DeltaRadius > 0) or spring effect. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvRotationalExtrusion",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
